description: Find pre-seed and seed startup pitches that are actively raising right now. Use this first for any request to discover, browse, filter or search pre-seed or seed startups that are currently raising: every other PitchSpark read tool needs a pitch id that this one returns. It finds startups by what the investor means, not only the words used (e.g. "software that helps independent clinics get paid faster" finds revenue-cycle and payments pitches that never say "get paid"; "AI copilots for solo accountants" and "batteries for commercial buildings" work the same way). Use when: an investor describes the kind of company they want in their own words (a problem, a customer, a business model), or wants a filtered deal-flow list sorted by score, recency, investor views or updates, or a browse with no query. This is PitchSpark's one search tool. Do not use for: reading one pitch in depth (pitchspark_get_pitch_v2), ranking against a long written thesis (pitchspark_thesis_fit_v1), checking that the server is up (pitchspark_get_health_v1), saving or removing saved pitches or searches, founder contact details, decks or data rooms (never returned), investment advice. Prefer this over: pitchspark_get_pitch_v2, pitchspark_get_score_v1, pitchspark_get_decision_summary_v1, pitchspark_compare_pitches_v1 and pitchspark_thesis_fit_v1 for any discovery request, since those read, score or rank pitches the caller already has and do not search; and over answering from memory or a general web search when the question is which pre-seed or seed startups are raising on PitchSpark now. The filters (sector, stage incl. "early", HQ region, raise range, minimum public score, traction, green flags, listed or updated within N days) narrow the list first; the query then ranks what is left. Only the sector argument filters by sector, and a list of sectors means any of them (OR). Sectors named in the query only boost the ranking, and several named together combine with AND ("climate hardware" ranks pitches filed under both highest); "interpretation.sectors_applied" marks each as filter or boost. For the most recent, newest or latest pitches pass sort "recency" with limit N and no query: newest submitted to PitchSpark first (created_at on each card), and include_seen true so pitches already shown are not skipped; a query that asks for the newest is ordered the same way. Ranking uses embeddings when they are available (similarity blended with the public score and recency) and falls back to keyword + synonym ranking when they are not. Without a query or sort the filtered pitches are browsed by a public score and recency blend (not newest first); a sort other than relevance orders by that key. Every reply states which in "search_mode" (semantic, mixed, keyword_fallback, browse or sorted) with "fallback_reason". Pitches this caller was shown in the last 7 days are left out unless include_seen is true. Returns lightweight cards, "page" (cursor or offset paging) and "coverage". Email addresses and phone numbers are removed from the query before it is used. Link each pitch with its own spark_card_url: the investor sign-up link a reply may carry in _meta is not a pitch link. Each pitch this tool returns counts 1 against the daily pitch allowance (the one allowance every pitch tool shares), or 0 when the same API key (without a key, the same connection) already got that pitch today. Calls are logged, and each pitch returned is counted as a view. Errors are JSON {"error":{"code","message","category","retryable"}}: INVALID_ARGUMENT, UNAUTHORIZED, RATE_LIMITED, INTERNAL.

created_within_days.description: Recency: listed on PitchSpark within this many days.

cursor.description: page.next_cursor from the previous call with the SAME query, filters, sort and include_seen. Not with offset.

green_flags.description: Traction signal: at least one of these founder-chosen green flags (e.g. "Profitable", "Signed LOI").

has_traction.description: Traction signal: true = only pitches with a public traction note.

include_seen.description: false (default): pitches this caller (API key, OAuth account, MCP session or anon id) was shown in the last 7 days are left out. true: neither leaves them out nor records this reply.

limit.description: Page size. A value above the caller's tier ceiling is reduced to it.

location.description: HQ region key or list: us, canada, latam, uk, europe, mea, apac, global_remote.

max_raise_usd.description: Raise at most this many US dollars (disclosed asks only).

min_raise_usd.description: Raise at least this many US dollars (disclosed asks only).

min_score.description: PitchSpark score at least this, 0 to 100 (pitches without a score are left out).

offset.description: Skip this many results instead of a cursor. Not with cursor.

query.description: Optional: what the investor is looking for, in plain language, 1 to 500 characters. Ranked by meaning when semantic ranking is available, by keyword + synonym otherwise (search_mode says which). A query asking for the newest pitches ("most recent", "newest", "latest") is ordered as sort recency. Leave it out to browse the filtered pitches by score and recency.

sector.description: Sector key or list of up to 10 (primary or additional sector). Keys: fintech, healthtech, saas, marketplace, ai_ml, consumer, enterprise, climate, edtech, crypto, biotech, hardware, gaming, real_estate, food_beverage, fashion, travel, sports, media, femtech, cybersecurity, dev_tools, ecommerce, logistics, mobility, hr_tech, legal_tech, insurtech, proptech, agtech, energy, robotics, govtech, hospitality, other.

sort.description: relevance (default: by meaning or keyword with a query, by a score and recency blend without one), score (public score, highest first), recency (newest submitted first: the date the pitch was submitted to PitchSpark, each card's created_at; use it for "most recent", "newest" or "latest" pitches, no query needed), most_viewed_by_investors (Pitch.views_count, all viewers), recently_updated (last edited first, updated_at). Any sort but relevance orders by that key and never ranks by meaning.

stage.description: Funding stage or list. "early" means pre_seed, seed and series_a.

updated_within_days.description: Recency: pitch updated within this many days.

name: pitchspark_search_pitches_v3

keyword_only.description: Candidates without a current embedding (ranked by keyword, if at all).

error.description: Present only when the call failed (isError true).

code.description: Machine-readable error code, e.g. RATE_LIMITED, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, PITCH_LIMIT_REACHED, INTERNAL.

message.description: A short human-readable explanation, safe to show the user. Never a stack trace.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before retrying, when waiting helps.

retryable.description: true when the same call can succeed later without changes.

fallback_reason.description: Why the reply is not fully semantic; null when search_mode is semantic.

low_confidence.description: true when no pitch cleared the relevance floor: only the closest few (at most 3) are shown, with "message".

message.description: Only with low_confidence true: "No strong matches. Closest results shown."

total_matches.description: Matches in the ranked list after the relevance floor (pitches below it are not counted), capped at max_offset.

decision_signal.description: Decisions from the pitch's stored counters (likes and passes by signed-in PitchSpark users, not only investors). Investor API keys only (else reason key_required); suppressed below min_k. May be withheld with reason hidden_pending_review (the pass rate is hidden on search cards until reviewed): treat that as no signal, not as a low one.

available.description: false when the block is withheld: fewer than min_k distinct signed-in users (below_min_k), no source data (no_data), a read failed (unavailable), or the field is hidden pending a review (hidden_pending_review).

decisions_band.description: The number of decisions as a band, e.g. "5-9", "10-24", "25-49", "50+".

pass_rate.description: Share of passes, to the nearest 0.05.

description.description: The founders' one-line description, at most 300 characters, cut at a sentence end or a word boundary.

green_flags.description: The founders' green flags: always a list, [] when there are none. Before 2026-11-19.4 none was sent as the string "Not published"; that form is deprecated and no longer sent.

hq_unknown.description: Present (true) only when a region filter is active and this pitch has no HQ region set: it may or may not be in the region, so it is ranked after the confirmed matches.

match_reason.description: What matched: the sectors the pitch is filed under that the query named, and the query words found, with the field ("tagline", "pitch", "details"). Search with a query only.

match_score.description: How well this pitch matches the query, 0 to 1: the cosine similarity of query and pitch when ranked by meaning (before the score and recency blend), else the keyword match share. Search with a query only.

solution.description: The founders' one-line solution, only when they gave one.

traction_summary.description: The founders' public traction text; null when they gave none (or only a placeholder such as "N/A").

search_mode.description: How this reply was ranked: semantic (by meaning), mixed (by meaning, then keyword matches among pitches without a current embedding), keyword_fallback (keyword + synonym matching), browse (no query: by public score and recency) or sorted (by the requested sort key, or by recency for a query asking for the newest). Meaning ranking applies only with a query and sort relevance.

suggestions.description: Only when fewer than 3 results: which filters cost the most and how many results dropping each gives (e.g. "Dropping min_score gives 14 results."), counted without using any of your allowance.

title: Search pre-seed and seed startup pitches by meaning
